molecules.simple: The potassium replenisher — corrects the dangerous-low potassium that causes weakness and arrhythmias, given slowly and always diluted.
molecules.how: IV never pushed — slow dilute infusion by staff; oral sachets/solutions with plenty of water.
molecules.alert: Rapid potassium infusion stops the heart — the dilution and pump-rate rules are absolute.

molecules.simple: The clotting vitamin — reverses warfarin effect and treats newborn haemorrhagic disease; the hospital antidote to over-anticoagulation.
molecules.how: IV (slow, diluted) or oral per INR protocol; newborns get a standard IM dose at birth.
molecules.alert: It takes hours to work — severe bleeds need clotting factors alongside, not vitamin K alone.

molecules.simple: Fish-oil triglyceride support — modest triglyceride lowering and heart-health support as an adjunct, not a replacement for statins or lifestyle change.
molecules.how: 1–4 g daily with meals per product strength and indication.
molecules.alert: Bleeding-time effects at very high doses are discussed with doctors on blood thinners.
brands: Seven Seas Cod Liver Oil Capsule

molecules.simple: A staph-specialist antibiotic cream — pierces impetigo, infected eczema and staph boils with a sterol-mimicking trick bacteria can't easily dodge.
molecules.how: Thin layer two or three times daily for 1–2 weeks.
molecules.alert: Resistance develops with underuse or overuse — finish the course, never share tubes.

molecules.simple: Antibiotic plus steroid eye drops — fights infection while calming inflammation in post-operative and mixed eye conditions, strictly under eye-doctor supervision.
molecules.how: One drop 3–4 times daily for the prescribed week; bottle never shared.
watch: Steroid effects on eye pressure with long use
molecules.alert: Steroid eye drops can worsen herpetic eye disease and raise pressure — ophthalmologist supervision is non-negotiable.

molecules.simple: Prostaglandin plus beta-blocker in one evening drop — outflow increased and fluid production reduced for stronger glaucoma control in a single bottle.
molecules.how: One drop at bedtime; inner-corner press after instillation.
molecules.alert: Asthma and heart-block cautions apply. Eye pain or vision change is same-day review.

molecules.simple: An India-born dual PPAR agonist — improves both sugar and triglycerides in diabetic dyslipidaemia, unique to the Indian market.
molecules.how: 4 mg once daily before breakfast; liver tests are monitored.
molecules.alert: Not for heart failure or significant liver disease. Long-term safety data is thinner than older classes — periodic review matters.

molecules.simple: A modern uric-acid blocker — stops the enzyme xanthine oxidase so gout crystals stop forming; the daily prevention tablet between attacks.
molecules.how: 40–80 mg once daily, continued between attacks; NSAIDs/colchicine cover the first months to avoid flare triggers.
molecules.alert: Heart-disease patients discuss risk (CARES trial signal). Starting it DURING an attack flares gout — timing matters.

molecules.simple: The classic uric-acid lowering tablet — reduces crystal formation for chronic gout and protects kidneys in tumour-lysis syndromes.
molecules.how: 100–300 mg daily titrated to uric-acid targets; same flare-cover rule as febuxostat; rash is the watchpoint.
molecules.alert: Blistering rash means stop immediately (SJS risk). interacts with azathioprine dangerously — dose coordination required.

molecules.simple: The ancient gout-relief alkaloid — stops neutrophils from attacking urate crystals, calming an acute attack within a day.
molecules.how: Low-dose regimens (e.g., 0.5 mg twice daily during flares) — dose-limited by diarrhoea; kidney dosing applies.
molecules.alert: Fatal interactions with statins and certain antifungals at high doses — full drug disclosure required.

molecules.simple: A sulfonylurea with a cardiovascular-friendly track record — pushes insulin release like glimepiride with a steadier profile.
molecules.how: Taken with breakfast; carry glucose for hypos.
molecules.alert: Severe kidney or liver impairment changes suitability. Hypo unawareness needs review.

molecules.simple: A meal-time insulin secretagogue — taken just before each meal, it produces a quick insulin burst matched to that meal and clears fast.
molecules.how: 0.5–2 mg within 15–30 minutes BEFORE each meal; skip the dose if skipping the meal.
molecules.alert: Same hypo cautions; interacts with gemfibrozil dangerously (skip that combination).

molecules.simple: A GLP-1 receptor agonist in tablet form — slows stomach emptying, curbs appetite and boosts insulin smartness, with strong heart-risk benefits.
molecules.how: Daily on an EMPTY stomach with a small sip of water, nothing else for 30 minutes — the rules protect absorption.
molecules.alert: Severe abdominal pain radiating to the back (pancreatitis) needs urgent care. Personal/family thyroid cancer history is screened first.

molecules.simple: A once-daily GLP-1 injection — proven heart protection and weight benefit in type 2 diabetes; also approved for weight management at higher doses.
molecules.how: Subcutaneous once daily, any time, titrated weekly as taught; rotate sites.
molecules.alert: Same pancreatitis and thyroid-history screening as semaglutide. Severe stomach pain = urgent review.

molecules.simple: An ultra-long basal insulin lasting beyond 24 hours — the flattest glucose profile with lowest nocturnal-hypo rates among basals.
uses: Type 1 and type 2 diabetes basal coverage
molecules.how: Once daily at ANY flexible time (its long tail forgives timing shifts); rotate sites.
molecules.alert: Never share pens or reuse needles. Missed doses are handled per the care team's plan, not doubled.

molecules.simple: Sugar-spiller plus liver-sugar-blocker in one tablet — dual mechanism with weight and heart bonus.
molecules.how: Twice daily with meals (metformin rule).
molecules.alert: Sick-day ketoacidosis rules of SGLT2 class apply — pause during severe illness.

molecules.simple: The original vessel-relaxing calcium blocker — strong pressure-lowering and anti-anginal action; SR forms for steady daily control.
molecules.how: SR once daily; short-acting forms are not for BP control (surge risk).
molecules.alert: Immediate-release capsules for urgent lowering are obsolete in routine care — they crash BP unpredictably.

molecules.simple: A reversible platelet blocker — faster onset and offset than clopidogrel, standard in acute coronary syndrome after angioplasty.
molecules.how: 90 mg twice daily (loading dose given in hospital); never stop without the cardiologist.
molecules.alert: Bleeding signs need urgent care. Aspirin is kept at low dose (75–100 mg) alongside — higher aspirin defeats it.

molecules.simple: A stronger irreversible platelet blocker — an alternative in stent patients when clopidogrel resistance is proven.
molecules.how: 5–10 mg once daily as part of dual therapy; bleeding history is screened first.
molecules.alert: Prior stroke/TIA contraindicates it. Age >75 or <60 kg uses the lower dose.

molecules.simple: A medium-length benzodiazepine — hospital favourite for acute anxiety, status epilepticus and alcohol-withdrawal protocols.
molecules.how: 1–2 mg as prescribed; injections are emergency-only by staff.
molecules.alert: Same dependence and tapering law as all benzodiazepines. No alcohol, ever, on it.

molecules.simple: A 1,5-benzodiazepine — calmer side-effect profile for seizure add-on therapy and anxiety, less hangover than classic benzos.
molecules.how: 5–20 mg daily in divided doses as titrated.
molecules.alert: Dependence rules apply. It can interact with valproate (rare rash syndrome in children).

molecules.simple: A COMT inhibitor that stretches each levodopa dose — fewer 'wearing-off' crashes in advancing Parkinson's.
molecules.how: 200 mg with EVERY levodopa dose; urine turns orange-brown (harmless).
molecules.alert: Never combined with non-selective MAO inhibitors. Liver tests on long courses.

molecules.simple: A selective MAO-B inhibitor — preserves the brain's dopamine in early Parkinson's and as wearing-off support.
molecules.how: 5 mg morning and noon (never late — insomnia); avoid pethidine and tramadol.
molecules.alert: Serotonin-syndrome risk with SSRIs/tramadol — full disclosure to every doctor.

molecules.simple: Levetiracetam's refined successor — same SV2A target with higher potency and fewer behavioural side effects for focal seizures.
molecules.how: Twice daily titration; converts from levetiracetam under neurology guidance.
molecules.alert: Same never-stop-abruptly rule. Mood or behaviour shifts are reported.

molecules.simple: A melatonin-agonist antidepressant — resets circadian rhythm while lifting mood, with essentially no sexual or weight side effects.
molecules.how: 25 mg at BEDTIME only (it works with the body clock); liver tests before and during therapy.
molecules.alert: Liver disease contraindicates it — LFTs are mandatory at baseline and at intervals.

molecules.simple: An SSRI with obsessive-compulsive superpowers — the classic OCD drug, also used in anxiety and depression.
molecules.how: 50–200 mg daily in divided or single evening dose, titrated.
molecules.alert: Strong CYP interactions (clozapine, warfarin, theophylline) — full disclosure required.

molecules.simple: The original antipsychotic — still used for severe psychosis, persistent hiccups and intractable vomiting in palliative settings.
molecules.how: 25–100 mg divided doses as prescribed; orthostatic dizziness common.
molecules.alert: Same NMS vigilance. Elderly and cardiac patients need careful review.

molecules.simple: An anti-fibrotic for pulmonary fibrosis — slows the scarring that stiffens lungs, preserving breathing capacity over years.
molecules.how: Titrated to 2400 mg/day in three doses with food; strict sun protection (photosensitivity).
molecules.alert: Sunscreen and clothing discipline is part of the therapy. Liver tests monitored.

molecules.simple: A triple-kinase anti-fibrotic — the second pillar of pulmonary-fibrosis therapy, slowing lung-function decline.
molecules.how: 150 mg twice daily 12 hours apart with food.
molecules.alert: Report severe persistent diarrhoea — dose pauses help. Bleeding risk reviewed with anticoagulants.

molecules.simple: An anticholinergic bronchodilator — opens airways by a different lever than salbutamol, and dries the runny nose of colds (nasal form).
molecules.how: Scheduled puffs/nebs as prescribed; not a rescue drug.
molecules.alert: Eye exposure of nebulised mist can precipitate glaucoma — mouthpiece preferred over mask.

molecules.simple: An anti-IgE biologic — for severe allergic asthma that ignores inhalers, it removes the antibody that triggers the reaction chain.
molecules.how: Every 2–4 weeks by weight and IgE level, clinic-administered.
molecules.alert: First doses are given where anaphylaxis can be managed — observation windows are standard.

molecules.simple: The classic overactive-bladder antimuscarinic — calms urge and urgency incontinence with affordable, effective dosing.
molecules.how: 5 mg two or three times daily, or ER once daily.
molecules.alert: Narrow-angle glaucoma contraindicates it. Cognitive fog in the elderly means switch, not push.

molecules.simple: Another prostaglandin glaucoma drop — once-nightly pressure control, sibling of latanoprost.
molecules.how: One drop at bedtime; lash growth/darkening expected.
molecules.alert: Same eye-emergency rules; adherence preserves sight.

molecules.simple: A carbonic-anhydrase-inhibitor drop — cuts the eye's fluid production, used alone or layered with other glaucoma drops.
molecules.how: One drop three times daily.
molecules.alert: Sulfa-allergic patients discuss cross-reactivity. Eye pain or vision change is same-day.

molecules.simple: An alpha-agonist glaucoma drop — reduces fluid production and boosts outflow; also useful after laser procedures.
molecules.how: One drop three times daily, spaced 8 hours.
molecules.alert: Not in infants/small children (dangerous CNS depression).

molecules.simple: An anti-VEGF eye injection — dries up the leaky, growing vessels that destroy central vision in wet macular degeneration and diabetic macular oedema.
molecules.how: Injected into the eye by a retina specialist every ~4–8 weeks per protocol.
molecules.alert: Escalating eye pain after injection = same-day retinal review. Adherence to schedule preserves vision.

molecules.simple: An anti-VEGF antibody — starves tumours of new blood supply in several cancers, and is used off-label inside the eye for retinal swelling.
uses: Wet AMD and diabetic retinopathy (off-label intravitreal)
molecules.how: IV infusion every 2–3 weeks per regimen; eye injections by retina specialists.
molecules.alert: Surgeries are timed around it (hold 4–6 weeks). Nosebleeds, BP spikes or proteinuria are monitored closely.

molecules.simple: A multi-kinase oral cancer drug — the standard tablet for liver cancer (HCC) and kidney cancer, slowing tumour blood supply and growth.
molecules.how: 400 mg twice daily on empty stomach; dose-pauses manage side effects.
molecules.alert: Painful palms/soles and BP rise are managed proactively — tell the oncologist early, don't endure.

molecules.simple: A kinase-inhibitor capsule for kidney cancer and GIST — dosed in 4-weeks-on/2-weeks-off cycles.
molecules.how: 50 mg daily on-cycle as prescribed; blood counts, BP and thyroid tracked.
molecules.alert: BP monitoring is part of the cycle; cardiac symptoms are reviewed promptly.

molecules.simple: The HER2-targeted antibody that transformed breast-cancer care — blocks the growth-receptor driving aggressive HER2+ tumours.
molecules.how: IV infusion every 3 weeks (or weekly) for a year in standard protocols; heart function (ECHO) is monitored throughout.
molecules.alert: Never combined with anthracyclines simultaneously (heart risk). Breathlessness or swelling gets same-day review.

molecules.simple: An anti-CD20 antibody — the B-cell eraser behind lymphoma therapy, rheumatoid and lupus protocols, and nephrotic-syndrome care.
molecules.how: IV infusions per protocol with premedication; first infusions are run slowly for reaction safety.
molecules.alert: Hepatitis-B screening before therapy is mandatory — reactivation is dangerous.

molecules.simple: A nucleoside-analogue chemotherapy — workhorse for pancreatic, lung, bladder and breast cancers in combination regimens.
molecules.how: IV infusion on weekly schedules per protocol with blood-count monitoring.
molecules.alert: Fever with neutropenia during cycles is an emergency (febrile neutropenia).

molecules.simple: A platinum chemotherapy for colorectal cancer — famous for cold-triggered nerve tingling in hands, throat and jaw during therapy.
molecules.how: IV infusion every 2 weeks per protocol; cold drinks/food avoided for days after doses.
molecules.alert: Numbness that lingers between cycles triggers dose adjustment — report early to preserve nerve function.

molecules.simple: A taxane chemotherapy — freezes cancer-cell scaffolds so they can't divide; used across breast, lung and prostate cancers.
molecules.how: IV every 3 weeks with steroid premedication (prevents fluid reactions).
molecules.alert: Fever in a chemo cycle is urgent (febrile neutropenia). Steroid premed schedules are followed exactly.

molecules.simple: The original platinum chemotherapy — cross-links tumour DNA; powerful in testicular, ovarian, lung and bladder cancers with strict hydration protocols.
molecules.how: IV per protocol with aggressive saline hydration and anti-emetics.
molecules.alert: Hearing changes and kidney parameters are monitored every cycle — hydration is not optional.

molecules.simple: Cisplatin's gentler sibling — kidney-sparing platinum dosed by kidney clearance (AUC), widely used in ovarian and lung cancers.
molecules.how: IV every 3–4 weeks, dose computed from kidney function.
molecules.alert: Platelet nadirs are watched; reactions after several cycles are discussed for premedication changes.

molecules.simple: A vinca alkaloid that paralyses cancer-cell division — a curative pillar in childhood ALL and lymphoma protocols.
molecules.how: IV push by oncology teams ONLY — intrathecal (spine) administration is a fatal error guarded against worldwide.
molecules.alert: New weakness, foot drop or severe constipation during therapy is reported immediately — dose adjustments protect nerves.

molecules.simple: A folate-pathway blocker chemotherapy — standard in non-squamous lung cancer and mesothelioma with vitamin cover.
molecules.how: IV every 3 weeks with B12 and folic-acid supplementation and steroid cover.
molecules.alert: Vitamin supplementation is mandatory — it protects against the worst toxicity.

molecules.simple: An androgen-receptor blocker for prostate cancer — sits on prostate cells' testosterone receptors, often alongside LHRH therapy.
molecules.how: One 50 mg tablet daily, same time.
molecules.alert: Yellowing or severe fatigue needs liver review. It potentiates warfarin — INR monitored.

molecules.simple: A hormone switch-off implant — a monthly/3-monthly pellet that shuts down oestrogen or testosterone production in breast and prostate cancer.
molecules.how: Subcutaneous depot every 4 or 12 weeks by staff; a brief initial hormone surge is expected.
molecules.alert: The first-weeks tumour flare in prostate cancer is anticipated and covered with other drugs.

molecules.simple: The anti-leprosy pillar — blocks folate pathways in Mycobacterium leprae; also used in dermatology for stubborn skin immune conditions.
molecules.how: Daily 100 mg within MDT for months; G6PD testing precedes use.
molecules.alert: Sore throat with fever on it = agranulocytosis check same day. G6PD deficiency causes haemolysis.

molecules.simple: The red MDT capsule for leprosy — anti-inflammatory and anti-bacterial; skin and eye reddish tint are its famous reversible mark.
molecules.how: Taken with food (absorbed in fat) monthly-supervised or daily per regimen.
molecules.alert: Intestinal deposits cause cramping pains on long use — reviewed by the treating team.

molecules.simple: A physical de-foamer — pops the surface tension of gas bubbles so trapped wind passes easily; no absorption, no chemistry, just physics.
molecules.how: 125 mg after meals and at bedtime; drops by infant dose with feeds.
molecules.alert: Persistent severe bloating with weight loss or pain is investigated, not just defoamed.

molecules.simple: Replacement digestive enzymes — lipase, amylase and protease taken with meals when the pancreas can't supply enough (chronic pancreatitis, cystic fibrosis, post-surgery).
molecules.how: Capsules with the first mouthful of every meal, dose titrated to stool comfort; not chewed or crushed.
molecules.alert: Stools that remain greasy/floating despite therapy need dose review by the gastroenterologist.

molecules.simple: Male-hormone replacement — restores testosterone in confirmed deficiency under endocrine supervision, with blood levels and haematocrit monitored.
molecules.how: Deep IM injections every 2–4 weeks per protocol; levels checked mid-cycle.
molecules.alert: Prostate screening precedes therapy. Never self-prescribed for gym/bodybuilding — real harms, real monitoring.

molecules.simple: An RANKL-blocker injection — every 6 months it stops the bone-dissolving cells, protecting bone in osteoporosis and cancer bone disease.
molecules.how: 60 mg SC every 6 months (osteoporosis) or monthly schedules in oncology; calcium and vitamin D run alongside.
molecules.alert: Missing a dose risks rebound vertebral fractures — schedules are strict; dental checks before long therapy.

molecules.simple: A thyroid-derived hormone that pauses bone breakdown and eases bone pain — now second-line for osteoporosis but still used for acute painful vertebral fractures.
molecules.how: Nasal spray daily or injections per protocol; courses are time-limited.
molecules.alert: Long-term cancer-signal concerns limit chronic use — short acute-pain courses only.

molecules.simple: A mineralocorticoid — makes kidneys retain salt and water to hold blood pressure up in adrenal failure and standing-BP-drop syndromes.
molecules.how: 0.05–0.2 mg daily; BP, weight and potassium tracked.
molecules.alert: Over-replacement causes hypertension and fluid overload — titrated against home BP readings.

molecules.simple: Body-identical cortisol as tablets — the replacement therapy for adrenal insufficiency, split to mimic the body's morning-high rhythm.
molecules.how: Split doses (largest on waking), doubled during illness per sick-day rules taught by the endocrinologist.
molecules.alert: Sick-day rules and emergency injection training are lifesaving for adrenal patients — never skip that education.

molecules.simple: Meloxicam in a topical gel — anti-inflammatory relief rubbed directly into knees, shoulders and joints without stomach exposure.
molecules.how: 2–4 g rubbed into the joint 2–3 times daily.
molecules.alert: Not on broken skin; wash hands after application.

molecules.simple: A muscle relaxant with vessel-widening bonus — relaxes spastic muscles without heavy sedation, popular for neck and back stiffness in Asian practice.
molecules.how: 50 mg three times daily after food.
molecules.alert: Driving caution until individual response is known.
